newsitem.title: USA: GM's earnings to be hurt by marketing costs.
newsitem.headline: GM's earnings to be hurt by marketing costs.

text.p: General Motors Corp. expects its fourth-quarter earnings to be below industry analysts' expectations due to higher incentives and advertising costs for new products, according to analysts briefed by GM officials on Wednesday.
The said the automaker expects profits equal to about 60 cents a share, compared with analysts' consensus estimate of around $1.00, they said.

GM spokeswoman Toni Simonetti declined to comment Thursday on the earnings estimate but said GM had told certain analysts that the company expected higher incentive spending and commercial expenses in the fourth quarter.
GM, which earned profits equal to $1.98 a share in the 1995 fourth quarter, is in the midst of launching 15 new models in North America -- about one-quarter of its product line.
GM also told analysts it is spending more for growth in the Asia/Pacific region and Latin America and expects an overseas sales mix that is more neutral than positive, Simonetti said.

One analyst who asked not to be identified said GM guided analysts downward to 60 cents a share from the $1.00 consensus because of the incentives and new model advertising in the United States, as well as higher start-up costs for Poland, Argentina, China and Thailand.
"Basically, they are expecting a temporary hiccup in the fourth quarter," the analyst said.

Both Goldman Sachs and Painewebber cut their estimates for GM's fourth-quarter earnings Thursday morning, according to sources at the Wall Street investment houses. Goldman cut its earnings estimate to 50 cents per share from $1.05, a source said, while Painewebber cuts its estimate to 15 cents from 50 cents, according to a source at the firm.
GM's stock lost 87.5 cents to trade at $53.625 after a delayed opening on the New York Stock Exchange.
